title: A Popular Joint Supplement Is Linked to Faster Dementia
hook: A large study tied glucosamine — a popular joint supplement — to a 25% higher chance of dementia and a faster slide to Alzheimer's. It's an association, not proof.
key_points: Glucosamine, a popular supplement for joint pain, was tied to faster progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's.
The study found a 25% higher likelihood of developing dementia among glucosamine users.
Researchers also found biological clues that might explain the link.
It's an observational association — not proof glucosamine causes dementia — but a reason to be cautious.
content_html: Glucosamine is one of the most popular supplements for achy joints, taken by millions. A major new study gives users pause: it links glucosamine to a 25% higher likelihood of developing dementia, and to a faster slide from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease.
extra_html: The researchers also turned up biological clues that might explain the connection. Two cautions: the study shows an association, not proof that glucosamine causes cognitive decline, and the supplement's benefits for joint pain are themselves modest and debated. Still, anyone taking glucosamine — especially with memory concerns — may want to discuss it with their doctor. Reported by ScienceDaily.

related.title: The Supplements Older Adults Actually Need
related.hook: For most older adults, the real question isn't which trendy supplement to take — it's whether you have a specific deficiency. B12, vitamin D, and often-overlooked protein are where it matters.

related.title: Keeping Your Brain Healthy
related.hook: No pill prevents dementia, but the habits that protect your heart turn out to protect your brain too.
